testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When driving, your mirrors should:

options.text: Not be used because they are distracting.
Not be used unless there is traffic.
Be checked regularly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be checked regularly.
questions.explanation: You must know what is happening around your vehicle at all times. Check your mirrors often.

questions.question: Distracted driving:

options.text: Only happens from physical distractions, not mental ones.
Gets worse when you pre-program radio stations.
Can be avoided by eating while driving.
Can be avoided by not having complex conversations while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be avoided by not having complex conversations while driving.
questions.explanation: To stay safe, do not have complex or upsetting conversations while driving. Pre-program your radio before you leave. Do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving. Mental distractions are just as dangerous as physical distractions.

questions.question: When carrying a wide load, you should:

options.text: Drive as fast as possible.
Get special permits and follow special rules.
Honk at other drivers to make them move.
Drive on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get special permits and follow special rules.
questions.explanation: Wide, long, or heavy loads need special permits. Drivers with these loads must follow special rules, such as driving only at certain times.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?

options.text: Before you start driving
While driving
When stopped at a traffic signal

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before you start each trip. If you have a trailer, make sure it is straight when you adjust the mirrors.

questions.question: Front wheel brakes work:

options.text: Only on dry roads.
In all conditions.
In all conditions except snow.

questions.correctAnswerText: In all conditions.
questions.explanation: Front wheel brakes work well in all road conditions. You are unlikely to have a front wheel skid, even on ice.

questions.question: When stopped on the side of the road, the driver should:

options.text: Keep their side door open.
Turn on their emergency flashers.
Wave their arms.
Turn off all their lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on their emergency flashers.
questions.explanation: If you stop on the side of the road, turn on your four-way emergency flashers to warn other drivers.

questions.question: When driving at highway speeds, you should watch the road about ____ ahead of your vehicle.

options.text: One block
100 yards
One quarter mile
One mile

questions.correctAnswerText: One quarter mile
questions.explanation: Look ahead 12 to 15 seconds to see obstacles and hazards. At highway speeds, this equals about a quarter mile.

questions.question: The tire load:

options.text: Can be exceeded in cooler weather.
Is the maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a given pressure.
Must be written in the shipping papers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is the maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a given pressure.
questions.explanation: Tire load is the maximum weight a tire can safely carry at a given pressure. This information is printed on the side of each tire.

questions.question: What is the number one cause of death and injury in work zones?

options.text: Speeding drivers
Careless behavior by construction workers
Drivers driving too slowly
Equipment placed in the roadway

questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding drivers
questions.explanation: Speeding is the main cause of death and injury in work zones. Drive carefully near road workers.

questions.question: A bridge formula:

options.text: Allows less weight per axle when axles are close together.
Allows more weight for trucks.
Is not a concern for drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows less weight per axle when axles are close together.
questions.explanation: A bridge formula sets the maximum weight allowed on each axle. Axles that are close together must carry less weight.

questions.question: If you use spring brakes while hauling a heavy load, how long will it take to stop completely?

options.text: It will be impossible to stop.
It will take a long time.
It will take a short amount of time.
It will damage the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: It will take a long time.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes turn on if air pressure gets too low in a vehicle with air brakes. A heavily loaded vehicle takes a long time to stop using only spring brakes because the spring brakes do not work on all axles.

questions.question: How many drinks does it take for a 200-pound person to reach a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.02 percent?

options.text: One
Two
Three
Four

questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Alcohol impairs your driving long before you reach the legal limit. A 200-pound person reaches a BAC of 0.02 percent after just one drink.

questions.question: How many hours of sleep does an adult need each night to stay alert?

options.text: Six to seven hours
Seven to eight hours
Eight to nine hours
Four to five hours

questions.correctAnswerText: Seven to eight hours
questions.explanation: Getting enough rest is important for safe driving. Most adults need seven to eight hours of sleep each night to stay alert.

questions.question: On a wet road, how much should you reduce your speed?

options.text: By about one-half.
By about one-third.
By about one-quarter.
By about one-eighth.

questions.correctAnswerText: By about one-third.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed by about one-third on wet roads. It is harder to stop or turn on slippery surfaces, so you must drive slower to stay safe.

questions.question: How can you reduce the amount of braking needed when driving down a hill?

options.text: Shift into a higher gear.
Shift into a lower gear.
Shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift into a lower gear.
questions.explanation: Before going down a hill, slow down and shift into a lower gear to help control your vehicle without using the brakes too much. Using the brakes too hard on a downhill can cause them to overheat and lose power.

questions.question: How should you brake if your vehicle's anti-lock braking system (ABS) is not working?

options.text: Brake normally. Your brakes will still work.
Pump the brake pedal repeatedly.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally. Your brakes will still work.
questions.explanation: Without a working ABS, your vehicle still has normal brakes. Drive and brake as you normally would. Have your ABS fixed as soon as possible.

questions.question: Which statement about the pre-trip vehicle inspection test is correct?

options.text: You do not have to identify the ABS.
You do not have to check the windshield wipers.
You only need to check shock absorbers on one axle.
You must check the steering box for leaks.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must check the steering box for leaks.
questions.explanation: During the outside inspection part of the pre-trip test, you must check that the steering box is mounted securely and is not leaking.

questions.question: When checking the fifth wheel gap during a pre-trip inspection, what should you look for?

options.text: A gap between the kingpin and the locking jaws.
The locking jaws fully closed around the kingpin.
The locking jaws loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: The locking jaws fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: When inspecting a tractor and trailer connection, look into the fifth wheel gap. Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.

questions.question: What does the suspension system do?

options.text: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
Keeps the load at the right distance behind the driver.
Keeps a safe distance between your vehicle and others.
Makes the load lighter for the tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up the vehicle and its load and keeps the axles in place. Damage to the suspension system is very dangerous.

questions.question: If your brakes fail on a downgrade, what is your best chance to stop?

options.text: An escape ramp.
Driving onto the shoulder.
Stay on the road.
Hit a slower vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: An escape ramp.
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail on a downgrade, use an escape ramp if one is available. If no escape ramp is nearby, look for another way to stop, such as a side road or open field.

questions.question: Your brakes need repair if the:

options.text: Brake pads are not covered in grease.
Brake pads are not covered in oil.
Brake pads are worn thin.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake pads are worn thin.
questions.explanation: When checking brakes, look for cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil or grease on them, and shoes that are broken or worn dangerously thin.

questions.question: On a 20-inch steering wheel, the maximum safe play is:

options.text: One-quarter of an inch.
Two inches.
10 inches.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two inches.
questions.explanation: A steering wheel with more than 10 degrees of play may be defective. On a 20-inch wheel, this equals about two inches of movement at the rim.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should stop shortly after driving to:

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are still tight.
Check that the tire is wearing evenly.
Check that the tire air pressure is correct.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are still tight.
questions.explanation: After driving a short distance with a new tire, stop and recheck the lug nuts to make sure they are tight.

questions.question: When turning to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Brake hard.
Not brake because it may lock the wheels.
Turn very sharply.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not brake because it may lock the wheels.
questions.explanation: Do not brake while turning quickly to avoid a hazard. Braking could lock your wheels and cause your vehicle to skid out of control.

questions.question: Friction inside a brake drum happens when the brake shoes and linings:

options.text: Push against each other.
Separate from the axle.
Push against the inside of the drum.
Create excess heat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push against the inside of the drum.
questions.explanation: Friction happens when brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: Before transporting an over-length load, you should:

options.text: Get special transit permits.
Alert fire departments along your route.
Pay tolls in advance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get special transit permits.
questions.explanation: Over-length, over-width, and overweight loads need special permits from the Department of Transportation.

questions.question: When backing a vehicle with a trailer, you should:

options.text: First turn the steering wheel in the direction of the turn.
First turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the turn.
Turn the wheel as sharply as possible.
Not use the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: First turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: With a trailer, turn the steering wheel opposite to where you want to go. Once the trailer starts to turn, turn the wheel the other way to follow the trailer.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, check that ____ engage automatically when air pressure drops below 45 psi.

options.text: Spring brakes
Parking brakes
Air brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Spring brakes
questions.explanation: Spring brakes should engage automatically when air tank pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi. Test this by chocking the wheels and releasing air from the brake system. When pressure gets too low, the parking brake valve pops out and spring brakes engage.

questions.question: To check automatic transmission fluid in some vehicles, the:

options.text: Vehicle should be parked uphill.
Vehicle should be parked downhill.
Vehicle must be washed.
Engine may need to be running.

questions.correctAnswerText: Engine may need to be running.
questions.explanation: Some vehicles require the engine to be running to check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: If a truck's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) fails:

options.text: The truck will have no brakes.
The truck should only be driven slowly.
The truck will still have brakes.
The truck will lose brakes on the left side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck will still have brakes.
questions.explanation: If the ABS system fails, the vehicle still has normal braking. Drive and brake as you normally would.

questions.question: Air tanks usually hold enough compressed air:

options.text: For one stop before needing to be refilled.
For several stops before needing to be refilled.
For a day's worth of braking.
For an unlimited number of stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: For several stops before needing to be refilled.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks can hold enough compressed air for the brakes to work several times before needing to be refilled.

questions.question: If a police officer asks you to take a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) test:

options.text: You can refuse to take the test without a penalty.
You can refuse to take the test but must pay a $50 fine.
You will lose your CDL if you refuse to take the test.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will lose your CDL if you refuse to take the test.
questions.explanation: Most states have an Implied Consent Law. By driving on state roads, you agree to take a drug or alcohol test if a police officer asks. If you refuse, you will lose your driving privileges. Know the laws in every state where you drive.

questions.question: Why should your mirrors show the road behind you and part of your vehicle?

options.text: Showing only the road in the mirrors would make the driver carsick.
Seeing part of your truck in the mirrors helps you judge distances.
It is illegal to show only the road in the mirrors.
You need to see the reflection of vehicles on the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Seeing part of your truck in the mirrors helps you judge distances.
questions.explanation: Part of your vehicle should be visible in your mirrors. This gives you a reference point to judge how close other drivers and objects are to your vehicle.

questions.question: Cargo inside a trailer:

options.text: Does not need to be secured.
Should be stacked no more than three feet high.
Should be secured to prevent movement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be secured to prevent movement.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be secured properly so it does not shift while you are driving.

questions.question: In a newer vehicle, the parking brake is applied by:

options.text: Moving a lever to the right.
Pushing a yellow, diamond-shaped knob.
Pulling a yellow, diamond-shaped knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pulling a yellow, diamond-shaped knob.
questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake has a yellow, diamond-shaped knob. Pull the knob to apply the brakes and push it to release them.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, weight should be:

options.text: Placed as high as possible.
Placed as low as possible.
Placed as far to the left as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Placed as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Heavy cargo placed high up makes a vehicle more likely to tip over. Place cargo as low as possible to keep the center of gravity low.

questions.question: To prevent your vehicle from rolling backward when you start to move, you can:

options.text: Partly engage the clutch before taking your foot off the brake pedal.
Place the vehicle in second gear.
Use the parking brake when stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Partly engage the clutch before taking your foot off the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To prevent your vehicle from rolling backward after stopping, partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal.

questions.question: How should you test the low pressure warning signal?

options.text: Engage and disengage the parking brake.
Rapidly press and release the brake pedal.
Open the rear shut-off valves.
Disconnect and reconnect all glad hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rapidly press and release the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: After the system is charged, test the warning signal by rapidly pressing and releasing the brake pedal. The warning light should come on when the air pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: An alcohol evaporator in an air brake system:

options.text: Makes the brakes work without squeaking.
Prevents ice from forming in the braking system.
Lubricates parts of the braking system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevents ice from forming in the braking system.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an evaporator that adds alcohol to the system. This alcohol helps prevent ice from forming inside the braking system.

questions.question: If you discover while driving that the ABS is not working, you should:

options.text: Turn on your hazard lights.
Downshift.
Brake normally.
Use the parking brake to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally.
questions.explanation: If the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is not working, your basic brakes still work. Drive and brake normally.

questions.question: What is true about a dual air brake system?

options.text: Each system has its own separate air tanks, hoses, and lines.
The systems share air tanks, but each has separate hoses and lines.
Both systems use the same lines and hoses.
One system is main brakes. The second system is a backup if the first fails.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own separate air tanks, hoses, and lines.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems. They share one set of brake controls, but each system has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: How long must carriers keep fuel records for IFTA quarterly fuel tax returns?

options.text: One year
Two years
Three years
Four years

questions.correctAnswerText: Four years
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles in interstate commerce must register under the International Registration Plan (IRP) and International Fuel Tax Agreement (IFTA). Carriers must keep mileage and fuel records for four years.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors?

options.text: Only when changing lanes
Frequently
Only if you think there is a problem

questions.correctAnswerText: Frequently
questions.explanation: You should check your mirrors often while driving. This helps you stay aware of traffic and notice any problems with your vehicle.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a problem when checking tires?

options.text: Too much air pressure
Too little air pressure
Using radial and bias-ply tires together
At least 2/32 inch of tread on rear tires

questions.correctAnswerText: At least 2/32 inch of tread on rear tires
questions.explanation: When checking tires, watch for air pressure that is too high or too low. Check that front tires have at least 4/32 inch of tread. Check that other tires have at least 2/32 inch of tread. Do not mix radial and bias-ply tires.

questions.question: What will you do during the vehicle inspection test?

options.text: Explain what you know about the pre-trip inspection process
Watch someone else check your vehicle
Watch a film about how to inspect a vehicle
Change all the tires on your vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you know about the pre-trip inspection process
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you will do a complete inspection of your vehicle. You will explain what you are checking and why.

questions.question: When making a tight turn in a CMV, what should you do?

options.text: Drive as fast as a car driver would
Focus on the road and do not worry about speed
Brake early and slow down gradually to warn drivers behind you

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake early and slow down gradually to warn drivers behind you
questions.explanation: Drivers behind you may not expect how slowly your CMV must go to make a tight turn. Brake early and slow down gradually to give them warning.

questions.question: How should you perform a driver's side parallel parking maneuver?

options.text: Pass the parking space while backing, then pull forward into it
Pull forward past the parking space, then back into it
Pull forward into the space without passing it first
Back into the space without passing it first

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the parking space, then back into it
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space to your left. Back into the space while moving the rear of your vehicle as close as possible to the rear of the space. Your vehicle must stay completely within the space boundaries.

questions.question: What does a modulating control valve control?

options.text: Spring brakes
Landing gear
Air brakes
Anti-lock braking system (ABS)

questions.correctAnswerText: Spring brakes
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets a driver apply spring brakes slowly and gradually. In vehicles with this feature, a lever on the dashboard controls the valve.

questions.question: Who is responsible for making sure cargo is loaded correctly?

options.text: The driver
The shipper
The recipient

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for inspecting the cargo, checking for overloads and unbalanced weight, making sure the cargo is secured without blocking their view, and ensuring cargo does not block access to emergency equipment.

questions.question: When carrying a sealed load, what should a driver do?

options.text: Open the load to check it for safety
Make sure the weight does not exceed legal limits
Go through the container before driving

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the weight does not exceed legal limits
questions.explanation: Although a driver cannot open and inspect a sealed load, they must still check that the total weight does not exceed the legal weight limits.
